Subject: Pricing exhibit: proposed credit-bridging & escrow language (Order Form v2)

Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Attached is Order Form v2 with the pricing exhibit (Exhibit B) updated to reflect the two items we discussed: 1) a short-term bridging credit for Q1 onboarding (to cover lower initial usage) and 2) a proposed escrow-style stability credit that would trigger if monthly usage drops below 40% of the committed baseline for two consecutive months.

High level: these are intended to be operational (billing) constructs rather than permanent changes to the rate card — they should let MediQuant trial aggressive adoption without losing the overall pricing economics for Redwood.

Can you ask your legal and procurement teams to: 1) review the new Exhibit B language (redlines attached), and 2) confirm whether an escrow-like credit account is acceptable operationally for you (we can wire a refundable credit or do monthly bill offsets).

If helpful, Neha is copied and can jump in on the billing mechanics and procurement checklist. I can also schedule a 30-minute call next week to go through redlines.

Attachments: OrderForm_MediQuant_Exhibit-Pricing_v2.pdf (pdf)

Jordan —

Thanks for sending. Our procurement team looked through the PDF and had two quick high-level questions before routing to legal:

- The "bridging credit" — will that be applied as a one-time invoice credit or spread over the first three invoices? Procurement prefers amortization across invoices (smoother impact on ARR) but wants to understand the mechanics.
- The escrow/stability credit — is Redwood proposing to hold cash in escrow, or would this be a syntactic construct (credit balance) Redwood maintains on our account? Holding actual escrow will require additional signoffs from our treasury.

We attached a short annotated PDF with procurement comments. If the escrow is a Redwood-held credit balance applied automatically, that will be much easier for us. Can Neha confirm?

Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement, MediQuant

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: proposed credit-bridging & escrow language (Order Form v2)

Tom —

Quick answers from billing/finance side:

- Bridging credit: default implementation is an amortized credit applied across the first three monthly invoices (we can make that explicit in Exhibit B). If you prefer a one-time invoice credit, we can do that but it will show as a larger single offset on month 1.

- Escrow / stability credit: Redwood prefers a ledger credit on the customer account (i.e., Redwood holds the balance and applies it to invoices if/when the trigger conditions are met). We only use third-party escrow for very large enterprise guarantees; for deals at this scale an in-account ledger is standard and avoids treasury-level approvals.

I've attached a short memo with suggested contract language to clarify both points for legal. Marissa — tagging you for any lawyer-level concerns on the Exhibit B wording, specifically around cap/floor mechanics and the treatment of credits on termination or assignment.

Neha Kapoor
Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[neha.kapoor@redwood.com]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@mediquant.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-26T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: proposed credit-bridging & escrow language (Order Form v2)

Tom / team —

Appreciate the procurement notes. A few legal redlines and suggestions below (high-level first, then specific redline snippets).

High-level concerns:
- Cap/Floor interplay: The current Exhibit B contains a "minimum monthly commitment" floor and a quarterly true-up. We should add explicit language that credits (bridging or stability) do not reduce the baseline for future true-ups unless both parties agree in writing. This prevents an unintended permanent shrink of the committed baseline due to temporary credits.
- Credit survivability / assignment: Clarify that any unused ledger credit at termination is refundable if Redwood has not applied it and the termination is for convenience by MediQuant; if Redwood terminates for cause, credits are forfeited. (We can negotiate a middle ground if they push back.)
- Measurement and dispute window: Define a 30-day window post-month for raising usage disputes before credits are applied.

Suggested contract snippet (to insert into Exhibit B):

"Bridging Credit Mechanics: The Bridging Credit shall be applied pro rata across the first three invoices following Effective Date unless the parties agree otherwise in writing. The application of Bridging Credits shall not be deemed an amendment to Customer's Baseline Commitment for purposes of any True-Up or Minimum Commitment calculation.

Stability Credit Account: Redwood will maintain a ledger account for Stability Credits. Stability Credits may be applied to reduce invoices as set forth in this Exhibit. Any Stability Credit remaining at the time of termination will be refunded to Customer within 60 days if Customer terminates for convenience. If Redwood terminates for material breach by Customer, any outstanding Stability Credit balance shall be forfeited.

Dispute Window: Customer shall have thirty (30) days following the issuance of a monthly invoice to dispute usage or credit application; absent timely dispute, the invoice and credit application shall be deemed accepted."

I'm attaching a redline of Exhibit B with the inserted language and two alternative formulations (one more customer-friendly: refundable on termination, one more Redwood-friendly: offset-only). Please review and let me know which lane MediQuant prefers so we can finalize.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal | Redwood Inference
[marissa.cole@redwood.com]

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: proposed credit-bridging & escrow language (Order Form v2)

Tom / Sylvia —

Thanks for the quick review and for flagging procurement's preference. We reviewed internally and proposed the following compromise:

- Bridging credit to be amortized across first three invoices (explicit in Exhibit B) — procurement win.
- Stability credit to remain a Redwood-held ledger credit that is refundable on Customer convenience termination (refund within 60 days) — gives MediQuant treasury comfort without third-party escrow.

Karthik is copied because there's a short commercial ask: to avoid creating a permanent downward adjustment to the baseline, we request language that any credit applied during the first 12 months will not reduce the annual committed baseline unless expressly agreed in writing. Karthik — can your team confirm the clean clause we should use for the final order form?

If that matches MediQuant's view, I'll ask Marissa to incorporate the agreed text and circulate the final Exhibit B for signatures. Propose a short call tomorrow 9am PT if you want to walk through the two redline options.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
